summary: Repeat prompt latency spike and intermittent timeouts due to KV/prefix cache miss behavior
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightCart dedicated tenancy) report higher-than-expected latency and intermittent request timeouts on repeated prompts (same prompt re-sent multiple times).

Impact:
- Several BrightCart production routes see 95th percentile token latency increase from ~120ms to ~450-700ms for repeat prompts.
- Intermittent 504/timeout errors for bursts of repeat traffic.
- Affects checkout recommendation and chat widgets; user-visible delays and dropped responses.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightCart) in us-east-1, production.
- Models: redwood-2-7b for interactive chat; redwood-14b for higher-quality reranking.
- Serving runtime version: 1.23.8.
- KV/prefix cache enabled with default TTL and automatic prefix eviction policy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a prompt A that primes a long prefix (multiple tokens) to redwood-2-7b in prod us-east tenancy.
2) Immediately re-send the exact same prompt A (repeat prompt) within <10s.
3) Observe latency for token generation on second request; compare p95/p99 against baseline.
4) Run at scale (burst of 50 concurrent repeat requests) and observe increased 504/timeout rate.

Observed logs/metrics:
- Serving runtime logs show extra KV cache lookup times (median 20ms -> 110ms under load) and increased backend fetches.
- Traces indicate fallback to cold KV population path causing synchronous disk/remote reads.
- Cache hit ratio for prefixes dropped from ~98% to ~67% for affected tenant during bursts.
- Errors: occasional 504s with upstream timeout message "kv-population-timeout".

Initial hypothesis:
- Regression in the prefix cache hot-path causes higher lock contention and synchronous cold-population during bursts, increasing per-request latency and causing timeouts.
- Possible related changes in commit range: PRs referenced above touching cache eviction/locking.

Attachments:
- Links to Grafana dashboards and traces included in related_confluence_pages.
investigation_notes:
2026-02-25 09:12 - Assigned to infra on-call. Collected flamegraphs and trace spans for affected tenant.
2026-02-25 11:30 - Confirmed elevated cache miss rate correlated with burst traffic patterns. Hot prefixes were evicted unexpectedly; eviction count spikes matched latency spikes.
2026-02-25 14:05 - Reproduced in staging with dedicated tenancy replica by running scripted repeat-prompt workload; observed same latency regression.
2026-02-26 08:40 - Scoped to concurrency handling: lock contention around prefix population path leads to synchronous disk reads. Suspect change in locking semantics introduced in serve v1.23.6 -> v1.23.8.
2026-02-26 12:10 - Cross-referenced SUP-1842 and SUP-2567 which describe similar behavior on other tenants; likely common root cause in shared serving runtime.

action_items: Create hotfix to revert lock escalation in prefix population path (ENG-#).
Roll out canary of hotfix to staging then to us-east dedicated pool for BrightCart.
Add instrumentation for prefix lock wait times and synchronous population counts.
Communicate temporary mitigation to BrightCart: enable eager prefix pre-warm or increase cache size quota.
Postmortem to be drafted after resolution and cross-tenant impact analysis.
resolution_notes:
2026-02-28 - Hotfix deployed (serve v1.23.9) reverting the lock escalation change. Canary in staging showed cache hit ratio restored to ~98% and p95 latency returned to baseline. Full rollout to BrightCart dedicated pool completed 2026-02-28 14:00 UTC.

Workaround used before fix: increased dedicated cache quota for BrightCart and enabled eager prefix pre-warm which reduced error rates.

Follow-up: Add SLA alerting for prefix cache hit ratio drop and include automated fallback to relaxed lock path if population latency exceeds threshold. Postmortem scheduled (linked in related_confluence_pages).
resolution_status: Fixed in serve v1.23.9; tenant restored to baseline performance
notes_for_followup:
- Track similar regressions across other dedicated tenants for next 2 weeks.
- Complete postmortem and publish runbook update for KV/prefix cache tuning.
- Consider automated cache pre-warm API for customers with bursty repeat prompts.
